query.historical_contract: [Discovery docs](https://open.umn.edu/opentextbooks/discovery): MARC, CSV, textbook/subject `.json`, RSS/Atom, deleted lists. Prefer import/local search.
query.refresh: Re-fetch permitted export with its robots pacing; validate size/schema/native identities and replace the research metadata snapshot atomically. Compare removed IDs with provider deletion notices. Never treat an unavailable export as an empty catalog.

licensing: Discovery page explicitly licenses catalog records CC0. Individual books have differing licenses including noncommercial/no-derivatives/GNU labels; no prose, full books or audio imported. A free-price metadata link is not proof of working access or reuse permission.
limitations: No CSV language field; a Spanish title or language-learning subject is not proof of content language. No India-origin/India-network coverage established.
Catalog contains paid print links alongside free digital links; research samples exclude paid/print links and label all reader destinations unverified.
Current export has 1,910 records; no claim every book is current, accessible, globally licensed or independent of existing sources.
Book reading, rights/version checks and provider numeric quota remain open. Ten searches verify catalog retrieval only.
next_action: Retain query-verified candidate; finish bounded PDF/representative reader checks, country/language evidence and refresh/deletion contract. Preserve CC0 metadata versus NC/SA book licenses and pedagogical versus practical intent.

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Twenty categories and how to find candidates for each
analysis_refs.text: | C04 Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters | DOAB publisher records, OAPEN, Open Textbook Library, open university presses and OER collections | NCERT, university presses, e-PG Pathshala, open course-text projects and state textbook bodies | Official exports/OAI-PMH plus bounded local search, or supported API; edition/chapter identity and per-book access |

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
All flags default off. No hosted Redis service or production deployment has
been created by this implementation. Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library and Book Dash use
bundled metadata and require no database. The reviewed StoryWeaver set also
searches locally, including ordinary Free to read searches when its flag is on. Live paper sources need the shared
Redis REST URL/token and a strong random `CONTENT_CURSOR_SECRET` (at least 32
characters), plus an explicit daily/minute budget for each enabled source.
The build's `VITE_CONTENT_DISCOVERY_ENABLED` controls the Search scopes.

analysis_refs.heading: Enablement
analysis_refs.text:
Enable `CONTENT_DISCOVERY_ENABLED`, `CONTENT_CHILDREN_ENABLED`,
`VITE_CONTENT_DISCOVERY_ENABLED` and `VITE_CHILDREN_PILOT_ENABLED` for the checked
preview/production build, with separate strong server-only cursor signing secrets.
This publishes Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library, Book Dash and the reviewed
StoryWeaver set. Source-account requirements remain visible.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase B — initial coverage
analysis_refs.text: Add Open Textbook Library, DOAJ and arXiv; OpenAlex after key/budget verification. Then DOAB/OAPEN imports and optional Unpaywall resolver with real contact email. Keep Google/Open Library enrichment bounded.

analysis_refs.heading: C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters
analysis_refs.text:
**Best starting points.** [DOAB metadata](https://doabooks.org/en/librarians/doab-metadata)
documents CC0 exports and OAI-PMH, including selective publisher/subject exports.
Use publisher identities to discover origins and verify their actual OA subsets.
[Open Textbook Library discovery](https://open.umn.edu/opentextbooks/discovery)
documents MARC/CSV, JSON resources and change feeds. Follow textbook publisher and
institution links into university presses and open-education programs. These
catalogs expose different kinds of books; keep textbooks, monographs and chapters
distinct even when the same publisher supplies all three.

analysis_refs.heading: Recommendation
analysis_refs.text: Start with **Free books** and **Research papers**. Add **Textbooks & learning** through the Open Textbook Library catalog, then a curated **Children's books** collection. Treat language, subject, reading level, format, and access conditions as separate filters rather than mutually exclusive categories.

analysis_refs.heading: Behavior
analysis_refs.text:
Ten new integrations are released behind `CONTENT_KNOWLEDGE_ENABLED=true`:
Global Digital Library, LibriVox, Library of Congress digital books, Biodiversity
Heritage Library's Internet Archive collection, African Minds, LSE Press,
Mattering Press, mediastudies.press, punctum books and Python 3.15 documentation.
Five publisher catalogs share Thoth; this is not five separate API infrastructures.
The existing Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library, Book Dash and StoryWeaver snapshots
and the existing OpenAlex/Europe PMC integrations are also selectable. With the
existing production flags, this gives 16 connected sources, not 16 fully audited
origins or complete catalogs.
